# `kernel/ProvenanceChecker.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/ProvenanceChecker.js`

ProvenanceChecker.js — SLSA-inspired build provenance validation. Signatures prove WHO built a package; provenance proves HOW. The 2026 TanStack attack shipped packages with valid signatures from a hijacked builder, so we validate a provenance block and (critically) that the declared source materials actually match the packaged files. Provenance block shape (in the envelope): { sourceRef:  'git@…#<commit>' | 'webgpu-os/devtools', builderId:  'webgpu-os/devtools' | 'ci/github', builtAt:    ISO timestamp, buildParams:{ … }, materials:  [ { path: 'files/app.js', sha256: '…' }, … ] } Returns a verdict { ok, level, builderId, warnings[] }: level 0 — no provenance (allowed, but lowers trust → risk badge) level 1 — provenance present + materials match packaged files level 2 — level 1 AND builder is a recognized trusted builder

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
